findings.title: Unknown receipt flags can be normalized into confirmed utility cleanup
findings.condition: Start with a complete positive original-utility receipt; set forcedStop to null at the aggregate and connection levels, or set spawnUnobserved to null while keeping complete:true.
findings.actual: qualifyMainUtilityClose returns state:confirmed in both cases. forcedStop uses ===true and therefore erases null/missing into false; complete accepts spawnUnobserved!==true rather than requiring an observed false.
findings.expected: Malformed or unknown authority/forced-stop fields retain unknown qualification; only explicit false permits positive qualification.
findings.impact: The retained JSON receipt validator can accept missing/unknown proof fields as successful utility closure. Current DesktopHost-generated DTOs emit explicit booleans, so this is a receipt validation defect, not evidence of a normal production installer bypass or native cleanup promotion.
findings.suggestion: Preserve malformed booleans as null in projection and require explicit spawnUnobserved:false and forcedStop:false for positive qualification. Keep valid original DTOs unchanged.

resolution.change: Malformed forcedStop values remain null; complete requires explicit spawnUnobserved:false; positive qualification requires explicit spawnAttempted:true. A valid original host DTO still confirms.
